title: Drift No More: Spectral Locking for Long-Horizon Open-Weight Multi-Agent AI
title_zh: 漂移不再：面向长程开放权重多智能体人工智能的谱锁定

paragraphs.en: 提出ATLAS在隐藏状态层面锁定任务、角色与状态子空间，无需训练即可显著抑制长程多智能体系统的漂移。 Long-horizon multi-agent systems suffer from three tightly coupled failures: task drift, role drift, and state staleness. We test the hypothesis that these share a common representational cause: agent hidden states move away from the directions encoding the active task, assigned role, and current shared state. A pilot study over 14,832 annotated turns supports this: drifted turns collapse near-uniformly across all three anchor subspaces (pairwise r = 0.72-0.78). Existing methods address these failures separately, operating at the surface-text level or treating control directions independently. We introduce ATLAS (Algebraic Task-role Locking with Adaptive Spectral Memory), a training-free intervention acting on hidden states before a token is generated. ATLAS builds a positive-semidefinite anchor kernel over task, role, and state subspaces and steers hidden states toward their shared high-coherence eigendirections; a low-rank Gram decomposition keeps this tractable. Across long-horizon memory, state maintenance, tool use, least-privilege coordination, and embodied stress tests, ATLAS outperforms prompting, retrieval, memory, and activation-steering baselines. Against A-MEM it improves memory macro-average accuracy by up to 5.7 points and reduces write/read failures by up to 31.7%/24.8%; against MemoryArena-Agent it gains up to 4.8 points. It gains 10.7-12.1 points under perturbation, reaches 93.5% role consistency, and transfers to a 72B backbone (macro-average 61.0 vs. 56.2). Ablating the joint task-role-state span costs 7.2 points against 0.8 for a matched-rank random span, indicating these directions are functionally implicated, not incidental; supplying them by prompt or retrieval recovers 4.3 points less. ATLAS is therefore a representation-level controller for open-weight multi-agent systems, complementary to output-level protocols for black-box agents.
paragraphs.zh: 提出ATLAS在隐藏状态层面锁定任务、角色与状态子空间，无需训练即可显著抑制长程多智能体系统的漂移。长程多智能体系统存在三个紧密耦合的失效问题：任务漂移、角色漂移和状态陈旧。 我们检验这样一个假设：这些问题共享一个共同的表征层面的原因，即智能体的隐藏状态偏离了编码当前任务、所分配角色以及当前共享状态的方向。 一项覆盖14,832个标注轮次的先导研究支持了这一假设：发生漂移的轮次在全部三个锚定子空间中近乎均匀地塌缩（两两相关系数 r = 0.72-0.78）。 现有方法分别针对这些失效问题，要么在表层文本层面操作，要么将各个控制方向独立处理。 我们提出ATLAS（Algebraic Task-role Locking with Adaptive Spectral Memory），这是一种无需训练的干预方法，在生成token之前作用于隐藏状态。 ATLAS在任务、角色和状态子空间上构建一个半正定的锚定核，并引导隐藏状态趋向其共享的高相干特征方向；低秩Gram分解使这一过程保持可计算。 在长程记忆、状态维护、工具使用、最小权限协调以及具身压力测试等任务上，ATLAS优于提示、检索、记忆和激活引导等基线方法。 相对于A-MEM，它将记忆宏平均准确率提升最多5.7分，并将写入/读取失败率降低最多31.7%/24.8%；相对于MemoryArena-Agent，它最多提升4.8分。 在扰动条件下它提升10.7-12.1分，角色一致性达到93.5%，并可迁移到72B骨干模型（宏平均61.0 对 56.2）。 消融联合的任务-角色-状态跨度会损失7.2分，而同等秩的随机跨度仅损失0.8分，表明这些方向在功能上确实相关而非偶然；通过提示或检索来提供这些方向，恢复效果少4.3分。 因此，ATLAS是面向开放权重多智能体系统的一个表征层面控制器，可与面向黑盒智能体的输出层面协议互补。
